      "title": "Retry-count cleanup is not limited to SMS reminders",
      "body": "The deleteMany query uses an OR branch with a bare `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` condition. That condition is not scoped to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`, so this SMS cron job can delete any WorkflowReminder row (including EMAIL or WHATSAPP reminders) once its retryCount exceeds 1. The retry-based deletion should be scoped to SMS reminders, and likely to unscheduled SMS reminders, to avoid deleting unrelated reminder rows."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts",

      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Reminders with no message or no sendTo never increment retryCount",
      "body": "When `message` is empty or `sendTo` is falsy, the code skips the SMS scheduling call but does not update `retryCount`, mark the reminder as failed, or delete it. Such reminders remain `scheduled: false` and will be selected again on every cron run until their scheduledDate passes. This preserves the endless retry behavior for bad/missing data that the PR is trying to avoid; these cases should also count as failures or be handled explicitly."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts",
      "line": 184,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "retryCount is updated using a stale read instead of an atomic increment",
      "body": "Both failure paths update with `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`, using the value read before the scheduling attempt. If two cron executions overlap or the same reminder is processed concurrently, both may read the same retryCount and write the same incremented value, losing a retry count. Using Prisma's atomic `{ increment: 1 }` would make the retry limit reliable. This also applies to the catch block update at line 195."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts",
      "line": 190,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Update inside catch can throw and abort processing of remaining reminders",
      "body": "The catch block awaits `prisma.workflowReminder.update` to increment retryCount, but this update is not wrapped in error handling. If the reminder was deleted between the initial `findMany` and this update (for example due to booking cancellation or concurrent cleanup), or if the update otherwise fails, the new exception escapes the catch block and stops the loop. That can prevent the remaining unscheduled reminders from being processed and cause the endpoint to return a 500. Using `updateMany`, ignoring not-found errors, or wrapping this update in its own try/catch would be safer."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts",
      "line": 195,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Any exception is treated as an SMS scheduling failure, including failures after Twilio scheduling",
      "body": "The catch block increments retryCount for every error, including errors thrown by the database update after `twilio.scheduleSMS` has already succeeded. In that case the Twilio scheduled message exists, but `scheduled` and `referenceId` may not be persisted, so the reminder remains unscheduled in the database and may be scheduled again on a later run. Repeated failures can also delete the WorkflowReminder while an externally scheduled SMS still exists. Consider distinguishing provider failures from persistence failures and handling/cleaning up the external scheduled message when the DB update fails."
    }

findings.title: Retry-count cleanup is not limited to SMS reminders
findings.body: The deleteMany query uses an OR branch with a bare `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` condition. That condition is not scoped to `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`, so this SMS cron job can delete any WorkflowReminder row (including EMAIL or WHATSAPP reminders) once its retryCount exceeds 1. The retry-based deletion should be scoped to SMS reminders, and likely to unscheduled SMS reminders, to avoid deleting unrelated reminder rows.

findings.title: Reminders with no message or no sendTo never increment retryCount
findings.body: When `message` is empty or `sendTo` is falsy, the code skips the SMS scheduling call but does not update `retryCount`, mark the reminder as failed, or delete it. Such reminders remain `scheduled: false` and will be selected again on every cron run until their scheduledDate passes. This preserves the endless retry behavior for bad/missing data that the PR is trying to avoid; these cases should also count as failures or be handled explicitly.

findings.title: retryCount is updated using a stale read instead of an atomic increment
findings.body: Both failure paths update with `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`, using the value read before the scheduling attempt. If two cron executions overlap or the same reminder is processed concurrently, both may read the same retryCount and write the same incremented value, losing a retry count. Using Prisma's atomic `{ increment: 1 }` would make the retry limit reliable. This also applies to the catch block update at line 195.

findings.title: Update inside catch can throw and abort processing of remaining reminders
findings.body: The catch block awaits `prisma.workflowReminder.update` to increment retryCount, but this update is not wrapped in error handling. If the reminder was deleted between the initial `findMany` and this update (for example due to booking cancellation or concurrent cleanup), or if the update otherwise fails, the new exception escapes the catch block and stops the loop. That can prevent the remaining unscheduled reminders from being processed and cause the endpoint to return a 500. Using `updateMany`, ignoring not-found errors, or wrapping this update in its own try/catch would be safer.

findings.title: Any exception is treated as an SMS scheduling failure, including failures after Twilio scheduling
findings.body: The catch block increments retryCount for every error, including errors thrown by the database update after `twilio.scheduleSMS` has already succeeded. In that case the Twilio scheduled message exists, but `scheduled` and `referenceId` may not be persisted, so the reminder remains unscheduled in the database and may be scheduled again on a later run. Repeated failures can also delete the WorkflowReminder while an externally scheduled SMS still exists. Consider distinguishing provider failures from persistence failures and handling/cleaning up the external scheduled message when the DB update fails.
